missionPremise: B-READER's own leave_behind, adopted verbatim: both production consumers of parcel_record claimed structurally-read-only with mechanisms weaker than a database role (parcelRecordFactRead.ts: code convention only; parcelRecordCellRead.ts: a protocol-level session flag, stronger but still credential-independent). Role-level read-only beats connection-level beats convention. Verify by violation at the database, never a code check. Role creation is a recorded store change through the sanctioned path.
completionPredicate: A SELECT-only role exists on the Factory Neon store, scoped to exactly the three tables named in the mission (the fourth, the verdict table, deferred -- see scopeBasis). A new distinct secret carries its connection string, never reusing or overwriting FACTORY_DATABASE_URL. Both named readers are swapped to it. An INSERT through the new credential fails at the database with a pasted verbatim refusal. The credential resolves correctly in the actual deployed Cloud Run environment (canary, digest-verified against the merge SHA, not merely locally). Role creation and every grant is recorded with its exact DDL and timestamp.
scopeBasis: Role and grants created live via psql against FACTORY_DATABASE_URL (rolcreaterole=true, verified before acting). Granted SELECT on parcel_record, parcel_record_cell, parcel_record_companion_row only -- NOT parcel_record_publish_verdict (B-GATE-SCHED's table), because that card's own migration is unmerged and, per a contract-mismatch finding filed as an addendum on parcel-b-gate-sched this session, targets a table shape that does not match B-READER's already-shipped contract; granting on a table whose final shape is still contested would need re-granting later. Code changes confined to the two named reader modules plus the one deploy-workflow secret binding; did not touch the allowlist, the verdict reader, or any rail-cutover logic (PARCEL_RECORD_SLATE stays empty, unchanged, per B-READER's own scope). Canary deployed and digest-verified; traffic was never shifted (no rail is live to serve differently either way).

verifyByViolation.note: Ran this exact test TWICE: once immediately after role creation (before the secret was persisted, to prove the mechanism before wiring anything downstream), and again against the FINAL persisted FACTORY_DATABASE_URL_RO secret value read back from Secret Manager, to prove the credential that ships is the one that was tested, not a discarded intermediate. Both refusals identical. The row named in the INSERT was never written -- Postgres checks privileges before constraint evaluation, so this is a clean permission-denied with zero side effects, not a rejected-but-partial write.

secretManager.whyTwoProjects: Discovered live, not assumed: the first canary deploy attempt FAILED with 'Secret projects/1062716564162/secrets/FACTORY_DATABASE_URL_RO/versions/latest was not found'. FACTORY_DATABASE_URL (the existing writer credential) is ALREADY mirrored into both projects -- confirmed live (gcloud secrets describe FACTORY_DATABASE_URL --project=legacy-design-tools-prod succeeds) -- and project-level IAM in legacy-design-tools-prod grants roles/secretmanager.secretAccessor to api-server-runtime@ and gha-deployer@ service accounts covering every secret in that project automatically, which is why the existing secret needed no per-secret IAM grant and why the new one only needed to exist there, not be individually IAM-bound. canaryDeploy.whyThisDoesNotFullyExerciseTheNewCode: PARCEL_RECORD_SLATE ships empty by B-READER's own design (no rail cut over yet, per _decisions/2026-09-02_step7_consumer_c_then_b.md) -- the allowlist checks slate membership synchronously BEFORE ever touching the verdict store or calling either reader, so there is currently no live HTTP path that invokes parcelRecordCellRead.ts or parcelRecordFactRead.ts's connection pool at all. This is a structural fact of the current program state, not a gap in this card: the strongest available verification is (1) the direct database-level violation test above, run against the real persisted credential, and (2) Cloud Run's own deploy-time secret-existence check, which is a genuine hard gate -- proven by the first deploy attempt failing loudly and specifically when the secret did not yet exist in the deploying project, not a check that could not have failed.

Whoever closes that reconciliation should also file a follow-up to grant parcel_record_ro SELECT on the correct, final table.

The two-project secret-mirroring pattern (hauska-prod-497015 and legacy-design-tools-prod both carry a live copy of every Factory secret cortex-api consumes) is undocumented anywhere in doc_repo prior to this close. Worth a canonical-doc note so the next card that mints a new Factory secret does not rediscover this by a failed deploy.

The new code path (RO-credentialed readers) cannot be functionally exercised via any live HTTP endpoint until a rail cuts over (PARCEL-B-SLATE1). This close's verification is therefore database-level plus deploy-time secret validation, not an end-to-end HTTP proof through the reader code itself. Whoever ships the first slate-1 cutover should treat that as the first true end-to-end proof of this credential.

LESSON: Cloud Run validates a --set-secrets reference's EXISTENCE at deploy submission time, before any container starts -- a missing secret fails the gcloud deploy command itself with a specific 'was not found' error naming the exact project number it resolved against, which is a fast, clear signal rather than a silent runtime failure.

This program's cortex-api service deploys into a DIFFERENT GCP project (legacy-design-tools-prod, 1062716564162) than the Factory store's own project (hauska-prod-497015, 172690833726). A secret minted only in the Factory project is invisible to that deploy. Existing Factory secrets (confirmed: FACTORY_DATABASE_URL) are already mirrored into both projects as an established, if undocumented, pattern.

legacy-design-tools-prod grants roles/secretmanager.secretAccessor at the PROJECT level to its runtime and deploy service accounts, not per-secret -- a newly created secret in that project inherits access automatically with no additional IAM step, unlike a fresh project with only per-resource bindings.

psql's `:'var'` interpolation syntax did not work via a single `-c` flag argument in this shell environment (syntax error at ':') but worked fine inside a heredoc passed to psql with no -c. Writing the DDL to a temp file with the value already substituted by the shell (not psql) and running `psql -f` sidesteps the whole question and is safer for a value with no special characters to escape.
DEAD-END: First canary deploy attempt with the secret existing only in hauska-prod-497015 -- failed fast and specifically, not silently; diagnosed from the error text alone, no guessing required.

psql -v pass="$PASS" -c "ALTER ROLE ... :'pass';" as a single command-line argument -- syntax error; the same variable-substitution syntax worked fine inside a heredoc in the earlier CREATE ROLE step. Switched to a temp SQL file with shell-side substitution instead of chasing why the two invocation styles differ.
